calculators.title: Car Trade-In Value Calculator
calculators.desc: Estimate a vehicle's trade-in value from original price, age, mileage, and condition.
calculators.formula: Estimated value = original price × age depreciation factor × mileage factor × condition factor.
calculators.example: A $40,000 vehicle that is 3 years old with 36,000 miles and good condition produces an illustrative market estimate.

calculators.title: F-150 Bed Dimensions
calculators.desc: Compare common Ford F-150 bed lengths and approximate inside bed dimensions.
calculators.formula: This is a specification lookup, not an arithmetic formula. Select a common bed length to view reference dimensions.
calculators.example: Choose 5.5 ft, 6.5 ft, or 8 ft to compare approximate inside length and cargo volume reference values.

calculators.title: Used Car Value Calculator
calculators.desc: Estimate an illustrative used-car value using age, mileage and condition adjustments.
calculators.formula: Estimated value = benchmark value × age factor × mileage factor × condition factor.
calculators.example: Use a realistic benchmark price and current mileage to compare how age and condition affect an estimated value.

calculators.title: Car Depreciation Calculator
calculators.desc: Estimate a vehicle's future value using an annual depreciation rate.
calculators.formula: Future value = current value × (1 − annual depreciation rate)^years.
calculators.example: A $35,000 car depreciating at 15% per year for 4 years is worth about $18,267 under this simplified model.

calculators.title: Car Resale Value Calculator
calculators.desc: Estimate a future resale value from current value, holding period and expected depreciation.
calculators.formula: Estimated resale value = current value × (1 − depreciation rate)^holding period.
calculators.example: Compare several annual depreciation assumptions to see a potential resale range.

calculators.title: Private Party Car Value Calculator
calculators.desc: Create an illustrative private-party value estimate using age, mileage and condition.
calculators.formula: Estimate = benchmark value × age factor × mileage factor × condition factor.
calculators.example: Start with a recent local-market benchmark rather than the original MSRP for a more realistic comparison.

calculators.title: Vehicle Payload Calculator
calculators.desc: Calculate remaining payload from GVWR, curb weight, occupants and cargo already loaded.
calculators.formula: Remaining payload = GVWR − curb weight − occupants − existing cargo.
calculators.example: A 7,000 lb GVWR vehicle with 5,000 lb curb weight, 400 lb occupants and 250 lb cargo has 1,350 lb remaining payload.

calculators.title: Truck Payload Calculator
calculators.desc: Estimate remaining truck payload after passengers and cargo.
calculators.formula: Remaining payload = GVWR − curb weight − occupant weight − cargo weight.
calculators.example: Use the door-jamb payload label when available because actual equipment changes curb weight.

calculators.title: Payload Capacity Calculator
calculators.desc: Calculate payload headroom for a loaded vehicle.
calculators.formula: Payload headroom = GVWR − curb weight − passengers − cargo.
calculators.example: This helps compare remaining capacity before adding hitch weight or additional cargo.

calculators.title: GVWR Payload Calculator
calculators.desc: Use GVWR and loaded components to estimate remaining weight capacity.
calculators.formula: Remaining capacity = GVWR − curb weight − occupants − cargo.
calculators.example: GVWR is a manufacturer limit; do not treat this calculator as permission to exceed axle, tire or hitch limits.

calculators.title: Trailer Weight Calculator
calculators.desc: Calculate loaded trailer weight from empty trailer weight and cargo.
calculators.formula: Loaded trailer weight = empty trailer weight + cargo + fluids/gear.
calculators.example: A 2,800 lb empty trailer carrying 1,000 lb of cargo has an estimated loaded weight of 3,800 lb.

calculators.title: Trailer Tongue Weight Calculator
calculators.desc: Estimate trailer tongue weight from loaded trailer weight and a target percentage.
calculators.formula: Tongue weight = loaded trailer weight × tongue-weight percentage.
calculators.example: At 12%, a 5,000 lb loaded trailer has about 600 lb of tongue weight.

calculators.title: Trailer Payload Calculator
calculators.desc: Calculate trailer cargo capacity from trailer GVWR and empty weight.
calculators.formula: Trailer payload = trailer GVWR − empty trailer weight.
calculators.example: A 7,000 lb GVWR trailer weighing 2,500 lb empty has about 4,500 lb theoretical payload before other limits.

calculators.title: Tongue Weight Percentage Calculator
calculators.desc: Calculate tongue weight as a percentage of loaded trailer weight.
calculators.formula: Tongue-weight percentage = tongue weight ÷ loaded trailer weight × 100.
calculators.example: 600 lb tongue weight on a 5,000 lb loaded trailer equals 12%.

calculators.title: Car Towing Capacity Calculator
calculators.desc: Compare a stated towing rating with GCWR-based remaining capacity.
calculators.formula: Estimated allowable trailer weight = min(manufacturer tow rating, GCWR − loaded vehicle weight).
calculators.example: If the tow rating is 7,500 lb but GCWR leaves only 6,800 lb, use the lower 6,800 lb before checking other limits.

calculators.title: Towing Capacity Calculator
calculators.desc: Estimate a towing ceiling using a manufacturer rating and GCWR headroom.
calculators.formula: Estimated towing ceiling = min(tow rating, GCWR − loaded vehicle weight).
calculators.example: Always also check hitch, axle, tire, payload and trailer ratings.

calculators.title: Car Fuel Cost Calculator
calculators.desc: Estimate fuel cost from trip distance, MPG and fuel price.
calculators.formula: Fuel cost = distance ÷ MPG × price per gallon.
calculators.example: 300 miles at 25 MPG and $3.50/gal costs about $42 in fuel.

calculators.title: MPG Calculator
calculators.desc: Calculate miles per gallon from miles driven and gallons used.
calculators.formula: MPG = miles driven ÷ gallons used.
calculators.example: 300 miles on 12 gallons equals 25 MPG.

calculators.title: Trip Fuel Cost Calculator
calculators.desc: Estimate road-trip fuel spending from distance, MPG and gas price.
calculators.formula: Trip fuel cost = trip miles ÷ MPG × fuel price.
calculators.example: Use round-trip mileage if you want a full-trip estimate.

calculators.title: Tire Size Calculator
calculators.desc: Calculate tire sidewall height, overall diameter and circumference from metric tire size.
calculators.formula: Sidewall = width × aspect ratio; diameter = wheel diameter + 2 × sidewall; circumference = π × diameter.
calculators.example: A 225/65R17 tire is about 28.5 inches in overall diameter.

calculators.title: Wheel Offset Calculator
calculators.desc: Estimate wheel offset from wheel width and backspacing.
calculators.formula: Offset (mm) ≈ (backspacing − nominal wheel centerline) × 25.4.
calculators.example: A wider backspacing measurement generally moves the mounting face outward relative to wheel centerline.

calculators.title: Wheel Backspacing Calculator
calculators.desc: Estimate wheel backspacing from width and offset.
calculators.formula: Backspacing (in) ≈ wheel centerline + offset(mm) ÷ 25.4.
calculators.example: Use manufacturer wheel drawings for exact fitment because nominal wheel width excludes outer lips.

calculators.title: Bolt Pattern Calculator
calculators.desc: Estimate bolt-circle diameter from lug count and adjacent-lug center distance.
calculators.formula: Bolt circle diameter = adjacent chord length ÷ sin(π ÷ lug count).
calculators.example: For five lugs, an adjacent center-to-center measurement can be converted to an approximate bolt-circle diameter.

calculators.title: Horsepower Calculator
calculators.desc: Calculate horsepower from torque and RPM.
calculators.formula: Horsepower = torque (lb-ft) × RPM ÷ 5252.
calculators.example: 300 lb-ft at 4,000 RPM is about 228.5 horsepower.

calculators.title: Power-to-Weight Ratio Calculator
calculators.desc: Calculate horsepower per pound and pounds per horsepower.
calculators.formula: HP/lb = horsepower ÷ weight; lb/HP = weight ÷ horsepower.
calculators.example: 300 hp in a 3,600 lb car equals 0.0833 hp/lb or 12 lb per hp.

calculators.title: Car Loan Payment Calculator With Taxes
calculators.desc: Estimate a monthly auto loan payment including sales tax, fees, down payment and trade-in.
calculators.formula: Financed amount = price + tax + fees − down payment − trade-in; payment uses the standard amortizing-loan formula.
calculators.example: Compare a 60-month and 72-month term to see how payment and total interest change.

calculators.title: Loan Payment Calculator
calculators.desc: Calculate the monthly payment and total interest for a fixed-rate amortizing loan.
calculators.formula: Payment = P × r(1+r)^n ÷ ((1+r)^n − 1).
calculators.example: A $25,000 loan at 7% APR for 60 months has a payment around the high-$400s per month.

calculators.title: Compound Interest Calculator
calculators.desc: Calculate compound growth with optional recurring monthly contributions.
calculators.formula: Future value combines compound growth of the initial principal with the future value of recurring contributions.
calculators.example: $10,000 at 6% for 10 years grows substantially more when monthly contributions are added.

calculators.title: Discount Calculator
calculators.desc: Calculate final sale price and savings after a percentage discount.
calculators.formula: Sale price = original price × (1 − discount percentage).
calculators.example: 20% off $100 gives a final price of $80 and savings of $20.

calculators.title: Salary Increase Calculator
calculators.desc: Calculate a new salary and annual increase from a percentage raise.
calculators.formula: New salary = current salary × (1 + raise percentage).
calculators.example: A 5% raise on $60,000 increases annual pay by $3,000 to $63,000.

calculators.title: Geodesic Dome Calculator
calculators.desc: Estimate hemisphere surface area and enclosed volume from dome diameter.
calculators.formula: For a hemisphere: surface area = 2πr²; volume = 2/3πr³.
calculators.example: A 20 ft diameter hemispherical dome has about 628 sq ft of curved surface area.

calculators.title: Geodesic Dome Size Calculator
calculators.desc: Estimate basic hemispherical dome area and volume from diameter.
calculators.formula: Radius = diameter ÷ 2; hemisphere area = 2πr²; volume = 2/3πr³.
calculators.example: Try multiple diameters to compare material area and interior volume.

calculators.title: Geodesic Dome Surface Area Calculator
calculators.desc: Calculate approximate curved surface area for a hemispherical dome.
calculators.formula: Curved surface area = 2πr².
calculators.example: A 30 ft diameter hemisphere has about 1,414 sq ft of curved surface area.

calculators.title: Geodesic Dome Material Calculator
calculators.desc: Estimate covering material from dome diameter and waste allowance.
calculators.formula: Material area = hemispherical surface area × (1 + waste allowance).
calculators.example: Add 10–15% waste for seams, trimming and mistakes depending on material.

calculators.title: Concrete Volume Calculator
calculators.desc: Calculate concrete volume in cubic feet and cubic yards for a rectangular slab.
calculators.formula: Volume = length × width × thickness; cubic yards = cubic feet ÷ 27.
calculators.example: A 20 × 10 ft slab at 4 inches thick needs about 2.47 cubic yards before waste.

calculators.title: Square Footage Calculator
calculators.desc: Calculate rectangular area in square feet.
calculators.formula: Square footage = length × width.
calculators.example: A 20 ft by 12 ft room is 240 sq ft.

calculators.title: Board Foot Calculator
calculators.desc: Calculate lumber board feet from thickness, width, length and quantity.
calculators.formula: Board feet = thickness(in) × width(in) × length(ft) ÷ 12 × quantity.
calculators.example: Ten boards measuring 1 × 8 × 10 ft total about 66.67 board feet.

calculators.title: Stud Spacing Calculator
calculators.desc: Estimate the number of wall studs from wall length and on-center spacing.
calculators.formula: Stud count ≈ ceil(wall length in inches ÷ spacing) + 1.
calculators.example: A 20 ft wall at 16 in on-center needs about 16 studs before corners, openings and special framing.

calculators.title: Roof Pitch Calculator
calculators.desc: Calculate roof pitch, slope percentage and angle from rise and run.
calculators.formula: Pitch ratio = rise ÷ run; slope % = ratio × 100; angle = atan(rise ÷ run).
calculators.example: A 6-in rise over 12-in run is a 6:12 pitch, 50% slope, about 26.6°.

calculators.title: Rafter Length Calculator
calculators.desc: Estimate common rafter length from horizontal run, rise and overhang.
calculators.formula: Rafter length = √(run² + rise²), with optional overhang added along the slope.
calculators.example: A 12 ft run with 6 ft rise has a base rafter length of about 13.42 ft.

calculators.title: Flooring Calculator
calculators.desc: Estimate flooring coverage including a waste allowance.
calculators.formula: Order area = length × width × (1 + waste percentage).
calculators.example: A 20 × 12 ft room with 10% waste requires about 264 sq ft of flooring.

calculators.title: Tile Calculator
calculators.desc: Estimate tile quantity from project area, tile dimensions and waste allowance.
calculators.formula: Tile count = project area × (1 + waste) ÷ area per tile.
calculators.example: For 200 sq ft using 12 × 12 in tiles with 10% waste, plan for about 220 tiles.

calculators.title: Tile Spacer Calculator
calculators.desc: Estimate tiles per row and joint count from row length, tile width and grout-joint width.
calculators.formula: Tiles per row ≈ floor((row length + joint) ÷ (tile width + joint)).
calculators.example: A 120 in row with 12 in tiles and 1/8 in joints fits about 9 full tiles before cuts.

calculators.title: Deck Board Calculator
calculators.desc: Estimate deck board count from deck width, board width and gap.
calculators.formula: Board count ≈ ceil(deck width ÷ (board width + gap)).
calculators.example: A 20 ft deck using 5.5 in boards with 1/8 in gaps requires roughly 43 boards across the width.

calculators.title: Voltage Drop Calculator
calculators.desc: Estimate DC or single-phase voltage drop using conductor resistance, current and one-way length.
calculators.formula: Voltage drop ≈ 2 × one-way length × current × conductor resistance per 1000 ft ÷ 1000.
calculators.example: Use the actual conductor resistance for the gauge and material you are evaluating.

calculators.title: Wire Size Calculator
calculators.desc: Suggest a basic copper wire size from current using a simplified reference ampacity table.
calculators.formula: The tool chooses the first reference gauge whose simplified ampacity is at least the entered current.
calculators.example: This is a planning aid only; installation requirements depend on insulation, temperature, terminals, bundling and code rules.

calculators.title: Breaker Size Calculator
calculators.desc: Estimate a minimum breaker size for a continuous load using a 125% planning factor.
calculators.formula: Planning current = continuous load × 1.25, then select the next standard breaker size.
calculators.example: A 16 A continuous load gives 20 A after the 125% factor.

calculators.title: Amps to Watts Calculator
calculators.desc: Convert amps and volts to watts for a simple DC or resistive single-phase calculation.
calculators.formula: Watts = volts × amps.
calculators.example: 10 A at 120 V equals 1,200 W.

calculators.title: Watts to Amps Calculator
calculators.desc: Convert watts and volts to amps for a simple DC or resistive single-phase calculation.
calculators.formula: Amps = watts ÷ volts.
calculators.example: 1,200 W at 120 V equals 10 A.

calculators.title: Electrical Load Calculator
calculators.desc: Estimate current from total watts and voltage, with an optional continuous-load planning factor.
calculators.formula: Current = watts ÷ volts; planning current = current × continuous-load factor.
calculators.example: 2,400 W at 120 V is 20 A; applying a 125% continuous-load planning factor gives 25 A.
